title: Wells Fargo & Military Warriors Support Foundation at the 2018 WHC Garden Brunch
description: As the WHC Garden Brunch celebrates its 25th Anniversary, we are proud to highlight the work of Wells Fargo and the Military Warriors Support Foundation.   Bob Woodruff of ABC News and Virginia Lt. Gov. Justin Fairfax were on hand to present Ret. Army Staff Sergeant Dominic Perrotte III and his wife Kayla with a 100% mortgage-free house.  Perrotte, who completed 3 tours of duty in Afghanistan and Iraq and was wounded in 2012 when his vehicle was struck by a roadside bomb, was awarded the home after completing the Wells Fargo and Military Warriors Support Foundation's Homes4WoundedHeroes' three-year financial mentoring program.  For more information, visit: https://www.wellsfargo.com/military/veterans/

asr.full_text: Hi everybody, welcome to the 25th annual. Garden Brunch. We try and every year make. This brunch be about something special. And less self-referential for all of us. And we really believe that there's one. Thing that unites this town, this. Community, and that's support for our. Military veterans and the brave men and. Women who fight for this country. So. Today we have very special programs. We're getting behind. We partnered with the Wells Fargo Military and Veterans Program. And the Military Warrior Support Foundation. I want to recognize somebody important in. The audience. Oh, here he is. Commander Alvarez Jr. Commander Alvarez is a Purple Heart and. Silver Star recipient and so much more. He's actually the first U.S. pilot that was shot. Down in North Vietnam and he spent eight years in a North Vietnamese prisoner. Camp and we are so glad that he is here with us today. Thank You commander for. Your service and thank you for being here and joining us to recognize these. Important veterans programs that mean so much to us. There's a lot of great journalists in the audience here but I don't think. Anybody who's been committed to covering the front lines like Bob has, and he put his life. On the line, and he was injured back in 2006 in Iraq, but he's not allowed that to stop him. It's kind of the fallout of that. He and his wife, after he got back and got back into health,. Started a foundation that's very much focused on veterans. So really driving to creating positive,. Healthy futures for our veterans. He has been there with them. He recognizes the sacrifice. That our folks make and the impact. So now it's my great pleasure to introduce Bob Woodruff,. Who came all the way from China today. Where he's been covering stories to be with us today. Thank you, Bob. I want to thank you for what you're doing,. And I really want to thank Wells Fargo. For what you're doing as well. You know, everybody talks about something,. But I've seen actual proof. I remember several years ago,. I went down to North Carolina. Where a good friend of mine, Dale Beatty,. Was helping to build a home for one of those wounded veterans. And right out there was not only the money from Wells Fargo,. But they were actually out there with their hands and their feet. To try to build this house themselves. So I have so much respect for Wells Fargo for doing this event as well. You know, Wells Fargo has been working with the military,. Warrior Support Foundations,. Homes for Wounded Heroes program to provide 100% of the mortgage. They're mortgage-free homes that go out to these veterans. They're the combat wounded veterans and also the Gold Star families as well. Now, once a veteran enters this program, they're awarded a home,. And the family moves in, beginning a three-year family and financial mentoring program. To help them with this transition to life outside of the military into our civilian world,. And also to ensure that they have the tools and the skills they need to maintain this house over a long period of time. Then after successfully completing the mentoring program, the foundation officially transfers the deed to the veteran. And then to date, Wells Fargo has donated over 350 homes and has spent a value of $55 million to build these homes for the veterans and the Gold Star families. They've actually done this in all 50 states of our country. So it's not just giving away homes, but it's also about providing quality and very long-term assistance for our veterans for many years to come. So joining me here today as well is a great man that I just met. He's Virginia's Lieutenant Governor Justin Fairfax, who also went to an amazing college known Duke, which I really like. I'm so honored to be here with you today, Bob. Thank you for that warm and generous introduction and for all of your great leadership on such an important issue. I have the distinct honor today as Lieutenant Governor of the Commonwealth of Virginia to recognize this extraordinary veteran and his wonderful family. They are from Hampton, Virginia, so I want to give them a round of applause. To start, they represent our Commonwealth and our country so well. And Dominic, thank you for joining me. Staff Sergeant Dominic Perotti joined the Army in 2005 as a heavy equipment mechanic. He served a total of three tours in Afghanistan and Iraq,. Where he helped recover the remains of fellow service members on the battlefield. This is his lovely wife, Kayla, by the way. I'm going to give Kayla a round of applause because we know that family served together. Kayla, thank you for your sacrifice. In 2012, Dominic was wounded when his vehicle was struck by a roadside bomb. It was so dangerous that he and his team had to stay on the battlefield for 30 hours before they could evacuate. After he retired from the Army, Dominic was ready to begin a new chapter in his life. He applied for the Military Warriors Support Foundation's Homes for Wounded Heroes program. Dominic, Kayla, and their beautiful son, Dominic IV, began their journey with the Military Warriors Support Foundation three years ago. Their mentor helped them make budgets, manage their finances, and get ready to become homeowners,. And also helped them through the many challenges of transitioning to life outside of the military. Dominic even got his boat captain's license and started a business offering deep-sea fishing charters. Earlier this year, the Parades graduated from the Foundation's mentorship program and earned the deed to their home, mortgage-free. And I think that deserves a round of applause. Congratulations to you all. And now on behalf of the Military Warriors Support Foundation and Wells Fargo,. I would like Staff Sergeant Perotti to please open the door. We have a surprise for you. So Dominic, open that door. So Jerry Quinn is going to, from Wells Fargo's Military Affairs Program Manager,. Is going to present to Dominic with the official deed. And then Andrea Dellinger right here. With the Military Warriors Support Foundation. Is presenting this flag. To fly right in front of that home when you get down. There, Dominic. Thank you, Bob. Kaylin and I would like to thank. You and everybody here. Today for the support you show. For veterans, for myself,. And sharing with the world. The good work that Balls Fargo. And Military Warriors Support Foundation has done for families like ours. Staff Sergeant Perotti, I want to congratulate you and Kayla. On participating and finishing the financial mentoring program. Through the Wounded Warriors Initiative. My understanding is you're going to be awarded a great new home in Hampton, Virginia from Wells Fargo. So congratulations on your great work. I also understand you're a great commercial fisherman,. And I hope I get a chance to go out fishing with you at some point. Thank you again for your service to our country. So our Homes for Wounded Heroes program is our pioneer program. Where we award mortgage-free homes to combat wounded heroes and gold star spouses. And they go through a three-year journey with us through a family and financial mentorship program. Where we help them really identify debt and home ownership. And Dominic and Kayla have been with us just over three years. And are receiving the deed. And it's exciting to watch all the debt they've paid off,. Along with the fact that he's taken. On the role of entrepreneur through the time. With the program. And I really do feel like we were. Able to help give him those tools to put in his toolbox. To find that next step in his future. We want to see our veterans that are coming home. Transition successfully and be those important contributors. To the communities that we know that they can be. You know, veterans serve in their communities,. Volunteer more frequently than the general public. It's because of that service, that commitment to service. That made them join the military in the first place. So we're just honored to serve them. As they come back and transition. And our military men and women in uniform,. Standing guard every night for us,. The ones deployed away from home,. Separated from their families. We need to take care of them too, and we need to ensure that they have the access to ensure. That their finances and their family are stable back here at home so that they can pay attention. To the most important mission they have at that time. It's life changing for me, my family, to Military Warrior Support Foundation and Wells Fargo. Thank you more than I can say thank you. You've changed our lives. You.

textual.context: Presented as a charitable veterans-support program during a 25th-anniversary Garden Brunch, with named organizational and public-figure participants; the records do not establish whether the program is being promoted to the general audience or merely discussed and presented ceremonially.
textual.potential_relevance: A substantial promised benefit—a mortgage-free home and deed—is explicitly linked to entering and successfully completing a multi-year mentoring program, creating a reward-and-condition relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: These records do not verify program eligibility, application procedures, property ownership, organizational identity, or whether the described outcome occurred beyond the source's account.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents a veterans-support ceremony involving Wells Fargo and the Military Warriors Support Foundation. The mortgage-free home and deed transfer are described as benefits within a family and financial mentoring program, rather than an investment return, payment demand, or request for private data. These details support an event and charitable-program presentation rather than a demonstrated deceptive solicitation.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central content is a general event and human-interest presentation about recognizing a veteran family and discussing a veterans-support program, rather than a demonstrated scam mechanism or an investment, credential, recruitment, or paid-guidance flow.
